title.zh: 卷一百〇二 列傳第三十二: 蕭奉先 李處溫 張琳 耶律余睹
title.en: Volume 102 Biographies 32: Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen, Zhang Lin, Yelu Yudu
title.raw: 卷一百〇二 列傳第三十二: 蕭奉先 李處溫 張琳 耶律余睹 Volume 102 Biographies 32: Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen, Zhang Lin, Yelu Yudu

sentences.zh: 蕭奉先李處溫張琳耶律余睹

translations.literal: Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen, Zhang Lin, Yelu Yudu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen, Zhang Lin, and Yelu Yudu

sentences.zh: 蕭奉先，天祚元妃之兄弟也。

translations.literal: Xiao Fengxian was the brother of Emperor Tianzuo's Primary Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fengxian was a brother of Emperor Tianzuo's Primary Consort.

sentences.zh: 外寬內忌。

translations.literal: Outwardly lenient, inwardly jealous.
translations.idiomatic: He was outwardly easygoing but inwardly jealous.

sentences.zh: 因元妃為上眷倚，累官樞密使，封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: Because the Primary Consort was the emperor's intimate favorite, he rose through offices to Privy Commissioner and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Primary Consort enjoyed the emperor's intimate favor, he rose step by step to Privy Commissioner and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 天慶二年，上幸混同江釣魚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing, the emperor visited the Hun Tong River to fish.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqing, the emperor went to the Hun Tong River on a fishing excursion.

sentences.zh: 故事，生女直酋長在千里內者皆朝行在。

translations.literal: By precedent, chiefs of the Raw Jurchen within a thousand li all came to court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, every Raw Jurchen chief within a thousand li was to present himself at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 適頭魚宴，上使諸酋次第歌舞為樂，至阿骨打，但端立直視，辭以不能。

translations.literal: At the Head-Fish Banquet, the emperor had the chiefs sing and dance in turn for amusement; when it came to Aguda, he only stood erect and stared straight ahead, declining on grounds of inability.
translations.idiomatic: At the Head-Fish Banquet, the emperor had the chiefs sing and dance in turn for his amusement. When Aguda's turn came, he merely stood erect and looked straight ahead, declining on the ground that he could not perform.

sentences.zh: 再三旨諭，不從。

translations.literal: Again and again the emperor instructed him, but he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him again and again, but he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 上密謂奉先曰：「阿骨打跋扈若此，可托以邊事誅之。」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly said to Fengxian: "Aguda is so overbearing as this; we may find a pretext in frontier affairs and put him to death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said privately to Fengxian, "Aguda is this overbearing. Find a pretext on the frontier and have him killed."

sentences.zh: 奉先曰：「彼粗人，不知禮義，且無大過，殺之傷向化心。

translations.literal: Fengxian said: "He is a crude man who does not know ritual and righteousness, and moreover has no great fault; to kill him would wound the hearts of those turning toward us.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian replied, "He is a crude fellow who does not understand ritual propriety, and he has committed no serious offense. To kill him would wound our policy of winning others to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 設有異志，蕞爾小國，亦何能為！」

translations.literal: Even if he harbors different intentions, what can this tiny little state do!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if he harbors other designs, what can this paltry little state accomplish!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 四年，阿骨打起兵犯寧江州，東北路統軍使蕭撻不也戰失利。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Aguda raised troops and attacked Ningjiang Prefecture; the Eastern Route Military Commissioner Xiao Tabuye was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Aguda raised an army and attacked Ningjiang Prefecture. The Eastern Route military commissioner Xiao Tabuye was defeated.

sentences.zh: 上命奉先弟嗣先為都統，將番、漢兵往討，屯出河店。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fengxian's younger brother Suxian as commander-in-chief, leading Khitan and Han troops to campaign against them, encamped at Chuhe Ford.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Fengxian's younger brother Suxian commander-in-chief and sent him with Khitan and Han forces to campaign against them, encamping at Chuhe Ford.

sentences.zh: 女直乃潛渡混同江，乘我師未備來襲。

translations.literal: The Jurchen then secretly crossed the Hun Tong River and, taking advantage of our army's unreadiness, came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen then secretly crossed the Hun Tong River and struck while our forces were unprepared.

sentences.zh: 嗣先敗績，軍將往往遁去。

translations.literal: Suxian was defeated; army officers often fled.
translations.idiomatic: Suxian was routed, and officers throughout the army took to flight.

sentences.zh: 奉先懼弟被誅，乃奏「東征潰軍逃罪，所至劫掠，若不肆赦，將嘯聚為患」。

translations.literal: Fengxian feared his brother would be executed and memorialized: "The eastern campaign's routed troops flee punishment and plunder wherever they go; if there is not a general amnesty, they will gather in bands and become a scourge."
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian, fearing his brother would be put to death, memorialized, "The routed troops of the eastern campaign are fleeing punishment and plundering wherever they go. Unless a general amnesty is granted, they will band together and become a menace."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嗣先詣闕待罪，止免官而已。

translations.literal: Suxian came to the capital to await punishment; he was only dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Suxian presented himself at court to await punishment and was merely stripped of his office.

sentences.zh: 由是士無鬥志，遇敵輒潰，郡縣所失日多。

translations.literal: From this the troops had no fighting spirit; meeting the enemy they would at once collapse, and prefectures and counties lost grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the troops lost all fighting spirit, collapsing at every encounter with the enemy, while prefectures and counties fell away day by day.

sentences.zh: 初，奉先誣耶律余睹結駙馬蕭昱謀立其甥晉王，事覺，殺昱。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fengxian had falsely accused Yelu Yudu of joining with the imperial son-in-law Xiao Yu in a plot to set up his nephew the Prince of Jin; when the matter was exposed, Yu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fengxian had framed Yelu Yudu for conspiring with the imperial son-in-law Xiao Yu to install his nephew the Prince of Jin as heir. When the plot was exposed, Yu was executed.

sentences.zh: 余睹在軍中聞之，懼，奔女直。

translations.literal: Yudu, hearing of it in the army, was afraid and fled to the Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu, hearing of this while still with the army, was terrified and fled to the Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 保大二年，余睹為女直監軍，引兵奄至，上憂甚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoda, Yudu served as Jurchen supervising commander, leading troops that arrived suddenly; the emperor was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoda, Yudu served as supervising commander for the Jurchen and led an army that appeared without warning. The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 奉先曰：「余睹乃王子班之苗裔，此來實無亡遼心，欲立晉王耳。

translations.literal: Fengxian said: "Yudu is a descendant of Prince Ban's line; in coming he truly has no intent to destroy Liao, but only wishes to set up the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian said, "Yudu is of the Prince Ban line. He has come with no real intent to destroy Liao, but only to install the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 若以社稷計，不惜一子，誅之，可不戰而退。」

translations.literal: If for the altars of state you do not spare one son and execute him, without battle Yudu will withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: If you reckon by the welfare of the state and do not spare a single son, execute him and Yudu will withdraw without a fight."

sentences.zh: 遂賜晉王死。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was thereupon granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Prince of Jin to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 中外莫不流涕，人心益解體。

translations.literal: Within and without the court none did not shed tears; popular sentiment grew ever more disintegrated.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the court and the realm there was not a dry eye, and popular morale fell further apart.

sentences.zh: 當女直之兵未至也，奉先逢迎天祚，言：「女直雖能攻我上京，終不能遠離巢穴。」

translations.literal: When the Jurchen troops had not yet arrived, Fengxian flattered Tianzuo, saying: "Though the Jurchen can attack our Supreme Capital, in the end they cannot stray far from their nest."
translations.idiomatic: Before the Jurchen armies had arrived, Fengxian played to Tianzuo's wishes, saying, "The Jurchen may be able to attack our Supreme Capital, but in the end they cannot stray far from their homeland."

sentences.zh: 而一旦越三千里直搗雲中，計無所出，惟請播遷夾山。

translations.literal: Yet in a single day they crossed three thousand li and struck straight at Yunzhong; with no plan to offer, he could only request removal to Jia Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a single stroke they crossed three thousand li and drove straight at Yunzhong. With no plan left to offer, he could only urge the emperor to relocate to Jia Mountain.

sentences.zh: 天祚方悟，顧謂奉先曰：「汝父子誤我至此，殺之何益！

translations.literal: Tianzuo only then understood, turned and said to Fengxian: "You father and son have misled me to this point—what good is killing you!
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo only then understood. He turned to Fengxian and said, "You and your sons have misled me to this pass. What good would killing you do!

sentences.zh: 汝去，毋從我行。

translations.literal: You go—do not follow on my march.
translations.idiomatic: Go. Do not march with me.

sentences.zh: 恐軍心忿怒，禍必及我。」

translations.literal: I fear the army's hearts will be enraged and disaster will reach me."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the troops' anger will turn on me and bring disaster in its wake."

sentences.zh: 奉先父子慟哭而去，為左右執送女直兵。

translations.literal: Fengxian father and sons wept bitterly and departed; attendants seized them and handed them to the Jurchen troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian and his sons departed in bitter tears, but attendants seized them and delivered them to the Jurchen army.

sentences.zh: 女直兵斬其長子昂，送奉先及次子昱於其國主。

translations.literal: The Jurchen troops beheaded his eldest son Ang and sent Fengxian and his second son Yu to their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen beheaded his eldest son Ang and sent Fengxian and his second son Yu to their ruler.

sentences.zh: 道遇我兵，奪歸，天祚並賜死。

translations.literal: On the road they met our troops, who seized them back; Tianzuo granted death to them both.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they met Liao troops, who seized them back, and Tianzuo ordered both men put to death.

sentences.zh: 李處溫，析津人。

translations.literal: Li Chuwen was a native of Xijin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chuwen was a native of Xijin.

sentences.zh: 伯父儼，大康初為將作少監，累官參知政事，封漆水郡王，雅與北樞密使蕭奉先友舊。

translations.literal: His uncle Yan, in the early Dakang era served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, rose through offices to Vice Grand Councilor, was enfeoffed Prince of Qishui, and was on close terms with the Northern Privy Commissioner Xiao Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yan, early in the Dakang era, served as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and rose through successive posts to vice grand councilor, receiving the title Prince of Qishui. He was on intimate terms with the northern privy commissioner Xiao Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 執政十餘年，善逢迎取媚，天祚又寵任之。

translations.literal: He held power more than ten years, skilled at flattery and currying favor; Tianzuo again favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He held power for more than ten years, skilled at flattery and ingratiation, and Tianzuo again showered him with favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 儼卒，奉先薦處溫為相。

translations.literal: When Yan died, Fengxian recommended Chuwen as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died, Fengxian recommended Chuwen for the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 處溫因奉先有援已力，傾心阿附，以固權位，而貪汙尤甚，凡所接引，類多小人。

translations.literal: Chuwen, because Fengxian had supported him with his power, devoted himself to fawning attachment to secure his position; his corruption was especially severe, and those he brought forward were mostly petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fengxian had backed him with his own influence, Chuwen devoted himself to fawning on him to secure his position. His corruption was especially flagrant, and nearly everyone he advanced was a petty schemer.

sentences.zh: 保大初，金人陷中京，諸將莫能支。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoda, the Jin people took Central Capital; none of the generals could hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoda era, the Jin captured Central Capital, and none of the generals could hold the line.

sentences.zh: 天祚懼，奔夾山，兵勢日迫。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was afraid and fled to Jia Mountain; military pressure grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo, in fear, fled to Jia Mountain as enemy pressure closed in day by day.

sentences.zh: 處溫與族弟處能、子奭，外假怨軍聲援，結都統蕭幹謀立魏國王淳，召番、漢官屬詣魏王府勸進。

translations.literal: Chuwen with his clansman younger brother Chuneng and son Shi, outwardly borrowing the Resentful Army's vocal support, joined with commander-in-chief Xiao Gan to plot setting up Prince Chun of Wei, summoning Jurchen and Han officials to the Prince of Wei's mansion to urge enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen, together with his clansman Chuneng and his son Shi, outwardly invoked the support of the Resentful Army and joined commander-in-chief Xiao Gan in a plot to install Prince Chun of Wei. They summoned Khitan and Han officials to the prince's mansion to urge him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 魏國王將出，奭乃持赭袍衣之，令百官拜舞稱賀。

translations.literal: As the Prince of Wei was about to go out, Shi took a ochre robe and clothed him in it, ordering the hundred officials to bow and dance in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Wei was about to emerge, Shi brought forward an imperial ochre robe and dressed him in it, then ordered the officials to bow and dance in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 魏王固辭不得，遂稱天錫皇帝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei firmly declined but could not, and thereupon styled himself Emperor Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: The prince firmly declined but could not refuse, and thereupon took the title Emperor Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 以處溫守太尉，處能直樞密院，奭為少府少監，左企弓以下及親舊與其事者，賜官有差。

translations.literal: Chuwen was made acting Grand Marshal, Chuneng director of the Privy Council, Shi vice director of the Palace Workshops; Zuo Qigong and below, and kin and friends who took part in the affair, were granted offices in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen was appointed acting grand marshal, Chuneng director of the privy council, and Shi vice director of the palace workshops. Zuo Qigong and those below him, along with kinsmen and allies who had taken part in the affair, received offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 會魏國王病，自知不起，密授處溫番漢馬步軍都元帥，意將屬以後事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei fell ill, knowing he would not recover, he secretly invested Chuwen as overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot forces, intending to entrust him with later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei fell ill and knew he would not recover, he secretly appointed Chuwen overall commander of Khitan and Han forces, intending to entrust him with what followed.

sentences.zh: 及病亟，蕭幹等矯詔南面宰執入議，獨處溫稱疾不對，陰聚勇士為備，紿雲奉密旨防他變。

translations.literal: When the illness grew critical, Xiao Gan and others forged an edict summoning the southern chief ministers to enter for deliberation; Chuwen alone claimed illness and did not respond, secretly gathering brave men as a guard, falsely saying he held a secret order to guard against other changes.
translations.idiomatic: As the illness grew critical, Xiao Gan and others forged an edict summoning the southern chief ministers to council. Chuwen alone pleaded illness and stayed away, while secretly gathering fighting men as a precaution, claiming he held a secret order to guard against any sudden move.

sentences.zh: 魏國王卒，蕭幹擁契丹兵，宣言當立王妃蕭氏為太后，權主軍國事，眾無敢異者。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei died, Xiao Gan mustered Khitan troops and proclaimed that the prince's consort Lady Xiao should be established as empress dowager to hold military and state authority provisionally; none dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei died, Xiao Gan rallied the Khitan troops and proclaimed that the prince's consort, Lady Xiao, should be made empress dowager with provisional authority over military and state affairs. No one dared object.

sentences.zh: 幹以後命，召處溫至，時方多難，未欲即誅，但追毀元帥劄子。

translations.literal: Gan by the dowager's order summoned Chuwen; as troubles were then many, he did not wish to execute him at once, but only demanded return and destruction of the commander-in-chief's commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the dowager's order, Gan summoned Chuwen. With troubles pressing on every side, he was not yet ready to have him killed, but only demanded that the commander-in-chief's commission be surrendered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 處能懼及禍，落發為僧。

translations.literal: Chuneng, fearing he would meet disaster, shaved his head and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Chuneng, fearing he would share in the disaster, shaved his head and took monastic orders.

sentences.zh: 尋有永清人傅遵說隨郭藥師入燕，被擒，具言處溫嘗遺易州富民趙履仁書達宋將童貫，欲挾蕭後納土歸宋。

translations.literal: Soon a Yongqing man named Fu Zunshuo, who had followed Guo Yaoshi into Yan, was captured and fully stated that Chuwen had once sent the Yizhou wealthy commoner Zhao Lüren with a letter reaching the Song general Tong Guan, wishing to take the Xiao empress dowager and surrender the territory to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a man of Yongqing named Fu Zunshuo, who had followed Guo Yaoshi into Yan, was captured and testified in full that Chuwen had once sent Zhao Lüren, a wealthy man of Yizhou, with a letter to the Song general Tong Guan, proposing to deliver the Xiao empress dowager and surrender the territory to Song.

sentences.zh: 後執處溫問之，處溫曰：「臣父子於宣宗有定策功，宜世蒙宥容，可使因讒獲罪？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager seized Chuwen and questioned him; Chuwen said: "My father and I had the merit of settling policy for Emperor Xuanzong; we ought to receive pardon generation after generation—how can we be made to suffer crime through slander?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had Chuwen seized and questioned him. Chuwen said, "My father and I earned merit by settling the succession for Emperor Xuanzong. Our house ought to enjoy pardon from generation to generation. How can we be condemned on the strength of slander?"

sentences.zh: 後曰：「向使魏國王如周公，則終享親賢之名於後世。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "If the Prince of Wei had been like the Duke of Zhou, he would ultimately have enjoyed the name of cherishing the worthy among kin in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager replied, "If the Prince of Wei had acted like the Duke of Zhou, he would have won lasting fame in later ages as a kinsman who cherished the worthy.

sentences.zh: 誤王者皆汝父子，何功之有！」

translations.literal: Those who misled the king were all you father and sons—what merit is there!"
translations.idiomatic: It was you and your sons who misled the prince. What merit do you claim!"

sentences.zh: 並數其前罪惡。

translations.literal: She also enumerated his former crimes.
translations.idiomatic: She went on to enumerate his earlier crimes as well.

sentences.zh: 處溫無以對，乃賜死，奭亦伏誅。

translations.literal: Chuwen had nothing to answer and was granted death; Shi also was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen had no reply and was ordered to take his own life. Shi was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 張琳，沈州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin was a native of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin was a native of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有大志。

translations.literal: From youth he had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he harbored great ambition.

sentences.zh: 壽隆末，為秘書中允。

translations.literal: At the end of Shoulong he served as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shoulong era he served as a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 天祚即位，累遷戶部使。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo took the throne, he was promoted in succession to Commissioner of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzuo acceded, he rose in succession to commissioner of the household bureau.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢南府宰相。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Southern Chancellery Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to chancellor of the Southern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，天祚之敗於女直也，意謂蕭奉先不知兵，乃召琳付以東征事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tianzuo was defeated by the Jurchen, he thought Xiao Fengxian did not understand warfare and summoned Lin to entrust him with the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Tianzuo's defeats at the hands of the Jurchen, he concluded that Xiao Fengxian knew nothing of warfare and summoned Lin to entrust him with the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 琳以舊制，凡軍國大計，漢人不與，辭之。

translations.literal: Lin cited the old regulation that on all great plans of army and state Han men did not participate, and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Lin cited the old rule that Han men were excluded from major military and state decisions, and declined.

sentences.zh: 上不允，琳奏曰：「前日之敗，失於輕舉。

translations.literal: The emperor did not assent; Lin memorialized: "Yesterday's defeat lay in acting rashly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept his refusal. Lin memorialized, "Our recent defeats came from acting rashly.

sentences.zh: 若用漢兵二十萬分道進討，無不克者。」

translations.literal: If two hundred thousand Han troops are used to advance by separate routes, there is none that cannot be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: If we deploy two hundred thousand Han troops along separate routes, there is no enemy we cannot overcome."

sentences.zh: 上許其半，仍詔中京、上京、長春、遼西四路計戶產出軍。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him half, and still ordered the four circuits of Central Capital, Supreme Capital, Changchun, and Liaoxi to reckon households' property for raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him half that number and ordered the four circuits of Central Capital, Supreme Capital, Changchun, and Liaoxi to levy troops according to household wealth.

sentences.zh: 時有起至二百軍者，生業蕩散，民甚若之。

translations.literal: At the time some were levied up to two hundred armies; livelihoods were scattered and ruined, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In some cases households were levied for as many as two hundred army units. Livelihoods were ruined and the people suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 四路軍甫集，尋復遁去。

translations.literal: The four circuits' troops had barely assembled when they soon fled again.
translations.idiomatic: The troops of the four circuits had barely assembled before they melted away again.

sentences.zh: 及中京陷，天祚幸雲中，留琳與李處溫佐魏國王淳守南京。

translations.literal: When Central Capital fell, Tianzuo visited Yunzhong, leaving Lin and Li Chuwen to assist Prince Chun of Wei in holding Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Central Capital fell, Tianzuo moved to Yunzhong and left Lin and Li Chuwen behind to assist Prince Chun of Wei in holding Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 處溫父子召琳，欲立淳為帝，琳曰：「王雖帝胄，初無上命；

translations.literal: Chuwen father and son summoned Lin, wishing to set up Chun as emperor; Lin said: "Though the prince is of imperial descent, at first there was no command from above;
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen and his son summoned Lin, intending to install Chun as emperor. Lin said, "Though the prince is of imperial blood, there has been no order from above;

sentences.zh: 攝政則可，即真則不可。」

translations.literal: regency is permissible, but taking the throne in fact is not."
translations.idiomatic: regency is permissible, but assuming the throne is not."

sentences.zh: 處溫曰：「今日之事，天人所與，豈可易也！」

translations.literal: Chuwen said: "Today's affair is given by Heaven and men—how can it be changed!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen replied, "What is happening today has the mandate of Heaven and the people. How can it be undone!"

sentences.zh: 琳雖有難色，亦勉從之。

translations.literal: Though Lin showed a troubled countenance, he also forced himself to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lin looked troubled, he reluctantly went along.

sentences.zh: 淳既稱帝，諸將咸居權要，琳獨守太師，十日一朝，平章軍國大事。

translations.literal: When Chun had styled himself emperor, the generals all held key power; Lin alone held Grand Preceptor, attending court once every ten days to oversee military and state great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chun had taken the imperial title, the generals all held the key posts of power. Lin alone retained the title grand preceptor, attending court once every ten days in name to oversee military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 陽以元老尊之，實則不使與政。

translations.literal: Outwardly they honored him as a senior elder, but in fact did not let him participate in government.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they honored him as a senior elder statesman, but in fact kept him from any share in government.

sentences.zh: 琳由是郁悒而卒。

translations.literal: Lin from this grew depressed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lin died soon afterward, worn down by resentment.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹，一名余都姑，國族之近者也。

translations.literal: Yelu Yudu, also named Yudugu, was of the near line of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Yudu, also known as Yudugu, was a close kinsman of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 慷慨尚氣義。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous and valued honor and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was openhanded and held honor and loyalty in high regard.

sentences.zh: 保大初，歷官副都統。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoda he served in office as deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoda era he served as deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其妻天祚文妃之妹，文妃生晉王，最賢，國人皆屬望。

translations.literal: His wife was the younger sister of Tianzuo's Literary Consort; the Literary Consort bore the Prince of Jin, the most worthy, and the people of the state all placed their hopes on him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the younger sister of Tianzuo's Literary Consort, who had borne the Prince of Jin, the most worthy of the princes, on whom the people of the realm had pinned their hopes.

sentences.zh: 時蕭奉先之妹亦為天祚元妃，生秦王。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Fengxian's younger sister was also Tianzuo's Primary Consort and bore the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Fengxian's sister was also Tianzuo's Primary Consort and had borne the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 奉先恐秦王不得立，深忌余睹，將潛圖之。

translations.literal: Fengxian feared the Prince of Qin would not be established and deeply envied Yudu, intending to plot against him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian, fearing the Prince of Qin would not succeed to the throne, deeply resented Yudu and began to plot against him in secret.

sentences.zh: 適耶律撻葛裏之妻會余睹之妻於軍中，奉先諷人誣余睹結駙馬蕭昱、撻葛裏，謀立晉王，尊天祚為太上皇。

translations.literal: It happened that the wife of Yelu Tage Li met Yudu's wife in the army; Fengxian prompted someone to falsely accuse Yudu of joining with the imperial son-in-law Xiao Yu and Tage Li in a plot to set up the Prince of Jin and honor Tianzuo as retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the wife of Yelu Tage Li met Yudu's wife in camp. Fengxian prompted an informer to accuse Yudu of conspiring with the imperial son-in-law Xiao Yu and Tage Li to install the Prince of Jin and elevate Tianzuo to retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 事覺，殺昱及撻葛裏妻，賜文妃死。

translations.literal: When the matter was exposed, Yu and Tage Li's wife were killed and the Literary Consort was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Yu and Tage Li's wife were executed, and the Literary Consort was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 余睹在軍中聞之，懼不能自明被誅，即引兵千餘，並骨肉軍帳叛歸女直。

translations.literal: Yudu, hearing of it in the army, feared he could not clear himself and would be executed; he immediately led more than a thousand troops, together with kin and military households, in rebellion back to the Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu, hearing the news in camp, feared he could not clear his name and would be put to death. He immediately led more than a thousand men, together with his kin and their military households, in flight to the Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 會大霖雨，道途留阻。

translations.literal: It happened that great soaking rains fell and the roads were blocked and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains fell and the roads became impassable.

sentences.zh: 天祚遣知奚王府蕭遐買、北宰相蕭德恭、大常袞耶律諦裏姑、歸州觀察使蕭和尚奴、四軍太師蕭幹追捕甚急。

translations.literal: Tianzuo sent the Xi Princely House intendant Xiao Xiamai, the Northern Chancellor Xiao Degong, the Grand Chamberlain Yelu Diligu, the Guizhou surveillance commissioner Xiao Heshangnu, and the Four Armies grand preceptor Xiao Gan in very urgent pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo sent Xiao Xiamai, intendant of the Xi princely house; Xiao Degong, northern chancellor; Yelu Diligu, grand chamberlain; Xiao Heshangnu, surveillance commissioner of Guizhou; and Xiao Gan, grand preceptor of the Four Armies, in hot pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至閭山，及之。

translations.literal: At Lü Mountain they overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: At Lü Mountain they overtook him.

sentences.zh: 諸將議曰：「蕭奉先恃寵，蔑害官兵。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated, saying: "Xiao Fengxian relies on favor and despises and harms officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: The generals debated among themselves, saying, "Xiao Fengxian trades on imperial favor and treats officers and soldiers with contempt.

sentences.zh: 余睹乃宗室雄才，素不肯為其下。

translations.literal: Yudu is a heroic talent of the imperial clan who from of old has been unwilling to be beneath Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu is a man of heroic talent in the imperial clan who has never been willing to bow to Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 若擒之，則他日吾輩皆余睹矣。

translations.literal: If we capture him, then another day we will all be like Yudu.
translations.idiomatic: If we capture him now, we ourselves will be hunted down tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 不如縱之。」

translations.literal: Better to let him go."
translations.idiomatic: Better to let him go."

sentences.zh: 還，紿雲追襲不及。

translations.literal: They returned, falsely saying pursuit and attack could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back and reported falsely that pursuit had failed to overtake him.

sentences.zh: 余睹既入女直，為其國前鋒，引婁室孛堇兵攻陷州郡，不測而至。

translations.literal: Once Yudu had entered the Jurchen, he served as their state's vanguard, leading Wanyan Wushi's troops to attack and take prefectures and counties, arriving without warning.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yudu had joined the Jurchen, he served as their vanguard, leading the forces of Wanyan Wushi to overrun prefectures and counties and strike without warning.

sentences.zh: 天祚聞之大驚，知不能敵，率衛兵入夾山。

translations.literal: Tianzuo, hearing of it, was greatly alarmed, knew he could not resist, and led his guard troops into Jia Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo was deeply alarmed when he heard the news. Seeing that resistance was hopeless, he led his guard into Jia Mountain.

sentences.zh: 余睹在女直為監軍，久不調，意不自安，乃假遊獵，遁西夏。

translations.literal: Yudu, serving as supervising commander among the Jurchen, long without transfer, felt ill at ease and, pretending to go hunting, fled to Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu served the Jurchen as supervising commander but long went without promotion and grew uneasy. Pretending to go on a hunting excursion, he fled to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏人問：「汝來有兵幾何？」

translations.literal: The Xia people asked: "How many troops did you bring?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xia asked him, "How many troops did you bring with you?"

sentences.zh: 余睹以二三百對，夏人不納，卒。

translations.literal: Yudu answered with two or three hundred; the Xia did not receive him, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu answered that he had two or three hundred. The Xia refused to take him in, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 論曰：遼之亡也，雖孽降自天，亦柄國之臣有以誤之也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Liao's destruction, though calamity descended from Heaven, was also because the ministers who held the state's power misled it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The fall of Liao, though disaster descended from Heaven, was also brought about by the ministers who held power in the state.

sentences.zh: 當天慶而後，政歸後族。

translations.literal: From the Tianqing era onward, government passed to the consort clans.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianqing era onward, power passed into the hands of the empresses' kin.

sentences.zh: 奉先沮天祚防微之計，陷晉王非罪之誅，夾山之禍已見於此矣。

translations.literal: Fengxian thwarted Tianzuo's plans to guard against troubles while small, brought about the Prince of Jin's execution without crime—the disaster of Jia Mountain was already foreshadowed in this.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian blocked Tianzuo's plans to crush threats while they were still small, engineered the execution of the innocent Prince of Jin, and the calamity at Jia Mountain was already foreshadowed here.

sentences.zh: 處溫副魏王以僭號，結宋將以賣國，跡其奸佞，如出一軌。

translations.literal: Chuwen assisted the Prince of Wei in usurping the title, joined with Song generals to sell the state—tracing his treachery and flattery, it was all one track.
translations.idiomatic: Chuwen backed the Prince of Wei in seizing an unlawful title and conspired with Song generals to betray the realm. Tracing his treachery and sycophancy, the pattern is all of a piece.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 天祚之所倚毗者若此，國欲不亡，得乎？

translations.literal: Those on whom Tianzuo relied and leaned were like this—if the state did not wish to perish, could it succeed?
translations.idiomatic: These were the men on whom Tianzuo relied. Could a state so governed hope to escape ruin?

sentences.zh: 張琳足足守位，余睹反覆自困，則又何足議哉！

translations.literal: Zhang Lin merely held his post, Yudu turned back and forth and trapped himself—what more is there worth discussing!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin merely clung to his office, and Yudu, shifting this way and that, brought ruin on himself—what more is there to say of either!
